r1.why: Two-stage absorption [6,7], enzymes break polymers to monomers [8], facilitated diffusion and active transport [9].

r2.why: Monokaryotic from spore, no sexual reproduction, dikaryotic fusion, fruiting bodies all in [4].

r4.why: Carbon-based pollutants and toxicity caveat [18,19], mycoremediation [20], mycofiltration [21,22], lignin in compost [25], backyard pile [26].

r5.why: 'For leather, mycelium is grown on ... sawdust' ties the solid-state fermentation process to leather; cited [33,34] never say it is for leather.

r6.why: Light, biodegradable, from waste [35], strength-to-weight and embodied energy [36], charring like timber [38], 70-75% at <=1500 Hz [39], 0.1-0.2 MPa drawback [44,45].
